ana_03.label: Missingness
ana_03.content: 98% of runs are tied to a registered runner (player_id); only 1.9% are guest runs. 96.8% of all runs carry a video URL — speedrun.com's video-proof requirement is enforced almost universally. 91.2% of runs have a known country, so country analyses cover roughly nine in ten runs. The columns with the highest missingness are the alternative timing fields (in-game timer missing on 88%, real-time-no-loads missing on 87%) because most games only use one canonical timing method.

ana_07.label: Category fragmentation per game
ana_07.content: The 100 games in our cut spawn 608 per-game categories — a mean of 6.27 and a median of 5 per game. The maximum is 31 (Super Mario Bros. Category Extensions, an entire 'category-extensions' pseudo-game whose purpose is to track exotic side-categories), then 27 (Granny: Legacy), 20 (Papa Louie Category Extensions; MX Bikes), 16 (Undertale). 19 games carry 10 or more parallel leaderboards. At the other end, 7 games carry exactly one category (Bloons Tower Defense 6, Subnautica 2 in Early Access, Roblox: Alone, Chase, Final Ninja Zero, and others — usually newer or smaller communities). The implication: 'world record' is not one thing, it is roughly six things per game, each with its own #1 runner.

ana_13.label: Granny: Legacy is a Slavic phenomenon
ana_13.content: The Granny: Legacy leaderboard is one of the most surprising regional concentrations in the dataset. Of its 1,245 distinct runners with a country, 533 (42.8%) are from Russia. ana_14.label: Platform share across all 61,797 runs
ana_14.content: Half of all runs in our top-100 cut were performed on PC (49.8% — 30,755 runs). The other half is fragmented across 65 distinct platforms: Web 7.4% (mostly browser games like Google Snake), Nintendo 64 6.7% (Mario 64 era), NES 6.3%, Android 5.6% (largely Granny: Legacy), Switch 5.2%, then a long tail. Mobile platforms (Android + iOS) collectively account for 7.7% of runs, mostly via the Granny/horror-mobile sub-economy. There are runs verified on platforms as obscure as 'Airplane Seats', 'Tiger', and 'Pong Consoles' — single submissions each.

ana_15.label: Emulator share peaked in 2018, halved by 2026
ana_15.content: Across all 61,797 runs, the share that were performed on an emulator (vs original hardware or PC-native) has a clear arc by year: 6.9% in 2015, climbing to a peak of 18.3% in 2018, then declining steadily — 15.9% in 2019, ~10% across 2020-2024, 8.5% in 2025, and 7.8% so far in 2026. The peak in 2018 reflects the era when emulator runs were broadly accepted on the most popular leaderboards; the decline is partly composition (more PC-native games entering the cut, with no emulator-vs-native distinction) and partly tightening rulesets on classic-console leaderboards.

data_table.description: Emulator share of verified runs by year, 2015-2026

ana_16.label: Super Mario 64 is still 91% Nintendo 64 — but 40% of those are emulated

ana_19.label: The labour distribution: top 5% of runners do a third of all runs
ana_19.content: The runs-per-runner distribution is extremely skewed. Among the 28,069 registered runners with at least one run, the top 1% (280 runners) contribute 16.5% of all runs. The top 5% (1,403 runners) contribute 33.7%. The top 10% contribute 44.6%. The top 50% contribute 76.8%. The median runner has just 1 verified run; the 95th-percentile runner has 6; the 99th has 17; the single maximum is 315 (Akuretaki). The Lorenz curve is sharper than most labour-market distributions in the wild and roughly matches the 'Pareto principle' for the top 20% (which contributes 57.7% of runs — closer to 60/20 than 80/20).

ana_22.label: Silksong Any% weekly submissions: launch spike, slow decay, March bump
ana_22.content: Hollow Knight: Silksong's Any% category opened on 1 October 2025 with 81 verified runs in its first week. The volume held above 40 runs/week for the first six weeks (44-81 each week), then settled into a 7-30 runs/week pattern through winter. There was a notable bump to 59 runs in the second week of January 2026 (probably new-year content and an AGDQ-adjacent push), then back to ~10-20 runs/week. The last full week before the fetch (18 May 2026) saw 29 runs — a small but real uptick.

data_table.description: Weekly Any% submissions for Hollow Knight: Silksong from launch

ana_24.label: Silksong median Any% time: 83 minutes at launch, ~65 minutes by spring 2026
ana_24.content: Track the median Any% submission time week-by-week and the community's collective speedup is visible. In the launch week (29 September 2025) the median Any% Silksong submission was 4,975 seconds — 82.9 minutes. By 10 November 2025 it had dropped to 68.4 minutes, by 2 February 2026 to 61.4 minutes, and by 2 March 2026 to 60.5 minutes. The curve roughly plateaued from there: the last several weeks in our cut sit in a 58-72 minute median band. Across eight months, the typical Any% submission shrank by about 22 minutes (a 27% reduction) — the route is now well-understood, and the gains are getting marginal.

data_table.description: Weekly median Any% submission time (seconds) for Hollow Knight: Silksong

ana_23.label: Silksong: Blue (Sweden) has a sub-60-minute run in the dataset
ana_23.content: Of the runners with the most Any% submissions for Silksong, the dataset's standout name is Blue (Sweden) — the same BlueSR whose pre-fetch news reporting set the Any% record at 1:03:41 in late 2025. In our snapshot Blue's best Silksong time across 4 submissions is 3,422 seconds: 57 minutes, well under the one-hour mark, and faster than any time reported in our pre-fetch sources. The other names at the top of Silksong's prolific list — meemeee (USA), CYV_ (Spain), IDAX1224 (China), 8Biggy (Quebec) — have submitted 5-9 runs each, several with sub-9-minute bests, which strongly suggests glitched or out-of-bounds sub-routes are mixed into the Any% category.

ana_25.label: Monthly verification volume across the top-100 cut, 2020-2026
ana_25.content: Total verified-run volume across all 100 leaderboards has grown roughly 10x from a 2020 baseline (155-500 verifications per month) to a 2026 ceiling (1,800-3,150). Three step-changes are visible: 2020-05 onward (early pandemic surge as people picked up speedrunning at home), 2022-05 spike (a single month at 1,604, which is hard to pin to one game), and the 2025-10 → 2026-03 ramp (driven primarily by Silksong's launch in September 2025 and the Granny: Legacy boom). March 2026 was the all-time peak month at 3,151 verifications.

ana_31.label: Granny: Legacy growth curve: 1 run to ~900 runs/month in 15 months
ana_31.content: The Granny: Legacy leaderboard opened in February 2025 with a single verified run. By month, the growth has been near-exponential: 4 runs in March, 12 in April, then plateauing for several months at 26-29/month through summer 2025. The jump came in October 2025 (68 runs), then 134 in November, 292 in December. 2026 has been: January 501, February 707, March 763, April 899 (peak month so far). The first three weeks of May 2026 saw 475 — pacing to match or beat April. Almost no other speedrun community in the dataset has grown this fast from a standing start.

caveats.content: The 'top-100 most-active' selection is by recent verification activity at fetch time (25 May 2026), not by historical fame. A different fetch date would produce a different cut. Inferences about 'what people speedrun' apply to this snapshot.
Runs.csv contains only per-game categories. Per-level (IL) categories were excluded from the fetch for size — IL runs would roughly double the run count for some games.

Within a per-game category, subcategory variables (e.g. 'Glitchless', 'Patch 1') further partition the leaderboard. A naïve cummin of time_seconds across a category mixes these subcategories together; this is why the Silksong Any% WR-progression shows 0-second / 15-minute glitch-route runs interleaved with 60-90 minute genuine runs.
1,161 runs are by 'guest' users without a player_id; these are excluded from per-runner analyses (top runners, Lorenz, monogamists) but included in per-game totals.
'Country' is the runner's self-reported country at fetch time; missing for 8.8% of runs. Country-of-WR analyses cover the 871 of 1,210 rank-1 rows with a known country.
May 2026 is a partial month at the time of fetch (25 of 31 days). Comparisons across April vs May should normalise to daily rates.
